name: E. G. Paddock
role: Medora livery stable owner, stockman and cattle buyer
bio: E. G. "Geary" Paddock was one of the early Little Missouri townspeople; a letter in one of the Cow Boy's first issues joked that he expected the paper to boom his town lots there. In March 1884 he sat on the five-man committee that drafted by-laws for the Bad Lands stockmen's association, and that May he, Lloyd Roberts and Dan Friedman brought 750 head of cattle from Minnesota for Rich, Randall & Co. From June 1884 into January 1885 he was among the signers of a standing $250 reward for information on anyone setting grass fires, and in late November 1884 he was elected to the school board. He won the first two Bad Lands Gun Club shoots for a rifle, in late February and early March 1885, and that spring opened a livery and sale stable in Medora that he soon planned to double in size; the April 1886 Billings County election was held in his livery office. In September 1885 the paper reported that the murder case against him and the Marquis over the killing of Luffsey had been moved to Bismarck on a change of venue, with both under arrest and bail refused, and later that month that he had been discharged. In October 1886 the paper noted him shipping cattle to St. Paul and visiting his old home at Wadena, Minn.
